issues.finding: The displayed equality repeats tf(and)(False,Undef) twice, leaving the symmetric argument order unshown despite the accompanying prose and the table's False/Undef and Undef/False entries.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use tf(and)(Undef,False) for the second expression.

issues.finding: The first listed formula has a closing parenthesis after q without a matching outer opening parenthesis.
issues.proposed_resolution: Add the outer opening parenthesis so the item is ((not p and p) implies q).

issues.finding: The source says not Diamond(p and not p) evaluates to Undef at p=Undef. Its own tables give p and not p = Undef, Diamond(Undef)=True, and not True=False.
issues.proposed_resolution: Give the displayed value as False; the claim that the formula is not a tautology remains valid.

issues.location: standard-language falsity constant in the Łukasiewicz matrix
issues.finding: The matrix names the standard propositional language L_0, defined earlier with a nullary falsity constant, but lists only four nonnullary connectives and supplies no truth value for that constant. A matrix requires an interpretation for every connective, including nullary ones.
issues.proposed_resolution: Include the falsity constant in the language item and set its logic-indexed truth-function value to False alongside the four tables.

translation_treatment: The target translates the full historical introduction, four connective truth-function tables over three truth values, exercises and modal critique, while correcting four bounded source issues. Frozen source is unchanged; inherited audits remain open.
